title: Rework lint suppression strategy, stage-aware cache validator, and shrink test footprint
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Refactor: centralize lint suppression into .lintrc, add stage-aware cache validator for presubmit and nightly lanes, split heavy integration tests into nightly suite to reduce presubmit time. Improves CI feedback latency and reduces flakiness by validating cache keys and avoiding brittle inline suppressions.
description:
Motivation: presubmit CI was increasingly noisy due to scattered lint suppressions and large integration tests running on every PR. This change consolidates suppression metadata, introduces a stage-aware cache validator (presubmit vs nightly) to reduce cache-related flakiness, and moves heavy/integration tests to a nightly lane while keeping a lightweight smoke suite in presubmit. Goals: (1) make suppressions auditable and reviewable, (2) lower presubmit run-time and flakiness, (3) catch cache key misconfigurations earlier with an automated validator, and (4) provide a straightforward path for dependency triage when linters fail.

What I changed (high-level): - Added .lintrc at repo root to centralize suppression rules and rationale (no inline // nolint in code); introduced lint-verify action that fails CI if inline suppressions are detected without a corresponding .lintrc entry. - Introduced ci/cache-validator: a small Go binary run as a presubmit check that verifies cache key stability across changed files and warns on keys that would cause cross-stage contamination (presubmit vs nightly). The validator runs in presubmit with strict checks and in nightly mode with wider heuristics. - Reworked github/workflows/presubmit.yml to:  * split tests into lanes: presubmit (fast unit + smoke), extended (optional on-demand), nightly (heavy integration).  * wire cache-validator into the presubmit fast lane. - Moved several slow integration tests into tests/integration/nightly/ and added a lightweight smoke wrapper tests/smoke/ that runs in presubmit. - Added docs/dev/ci-lint-guidelines.md describing the suppression policy, how to add entries to .lintrc, and expected review process. - Added a small dep-triage script (scripts/dep-triage.sh) that suggests minimal dependency bump candidates when linter rules fail due to third-party API changes.

Commits summary: squash of 7 logical commits: - centralize-lint-suppressions: add .lintrc and lint verifier - add-cache-validator: initial Go validator and unit tests - presubmit-yaml-split: stage-aware workflow lanes and lightweight smoke-run - move-integration-tests: relocate heavy tests to nightly folder - docs-ci-lint: add guidelines and example entries - dep-triage-script: helper script + README - fix-ci-flaky: follow-up adjustments after first CI run

Changed areas (representative files): - .lintrc (new) - github/workflows/presubmit.yml (modified) - github/workflows/nightly-integration.yml (new) - tools/ci/cache-validator/main.go (new) - tests/integration/nightly/* (moved) - tests/smoke/* (new minimal smoke tests) - docs/dev/ci-lint-guidelines.md (new) - scripts/dep-triage.sh (new) - Makefile / build/test runners (small targets added)

Testing and verification: - Local: ran lint-verify and cache-validator against a sandbox repo state and added unit tests for cache-validator with mocked cache-key scenarios. - CI: initial presubmit run failed due to a few inline suppressions left in legacy modules; those were converted to .lintrc entries and documented. After fixes, full presubmit CI passed (see CI checks). Nightly workflow validated integration moves in scheduled run.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: reviewers may miss rationale behind suppressions. Mitigation: .lintrc requires a minimal rationale string and a reviewer tag; docs include examples and we added a small presubmit warning when new entries are added. - Risk: cache-validator false positives. Mitigation: validator runs in warning mode for the first week in nightly lane and strict mode in presubmit only after two consecutive green runs in nightly. This PR enables strict presubmit only after rollout tag in the workflow.

Follow-ups (future work): - Wire dependent triage suggestions into the PR UI or a GitHub app for automatic suggestions. - Add an optional premerge job to auto-squash trivial lint-only fixes (requires policy decision). - Migrate remaining legacy modules to the new smoke test harness.

dep-triage-script: helper to propose minimal dependency bumps
fix-ci-flaky: small follow-up adjustments after CI feedback
reviews: Diego Alvarez (request changes): Please add a small ignore list for vendor/ generated files; we saw some false positives during local runs.
Maya Chen (author reply): Added vendor/ pattern to the verifier and included an opt-out note in the docs. PTAL.
Priya Nair (comment): Cache validator looks good, but can we limit the memory footprint on small runners?
Maya Chen (author reply): Validator already has a --mode=light option and uses streaming; documented in tools/ci/README.md. Added workflow flag to use light mode on tiny runners.
Ethan Glass (approval): Verified presubmit runtime dropped from ~22m to ~9m on my branch; approve.
Repo Admin (merge): Squash-merged after CI green and approvals.
ci_checks: presubmit: initial run - failed (inline suppression detections) - annotations added
nightly-integration: scheduled dry-run - pass (validator warning mode)
notes: Rollout: this PR flips strict presubmit validation off-by-default until next release window. The presubmit workflow contains a 'strict=true' flag gated by release tag.
Observability: added a small metric (ci.cache_validator.false_positives) to help tune heuristics.
Ops: SRE asked to watch nightly flakiness for one week post-merge; alert runbook updated.
